land.text: the post-palatial Mycenaean world: mainland, Crete and the islands

predecessors.note: The Mycenaean page ends its period c. 1050 BC and this page begins c. 1180; Cliopatria's -1100 handover is kept.

land.text: the Greek world of the poleis at the start of the Archaic period, 'c. 800 BC'

successors.note: Cliopatria's first Greek City-States shape (-800, 58,485 km2) has the same bounding box as this row's last shape.

capitals.name: Athens
capitals.note: No capital: the period had none. Athens is one of the four Early Iron Age (1050-800 BC) centres the page names (Lefkandi, Athens, Argos, Knossos) and the one whose acropolis 'appears to have avoided destruction' (Mycenaean Greece page); it anchors the label only.

keyframe_review.note: 49,236 km2: Cliopatria's Mycenaean -1150 shape less 40 cells (about 10,000 km2: the Aetolian, Evrytanian and Phthiotid interior and western Thessaly, 21.1-22.5 E, 38.6-39.6 N, and four Cycladic cells and Kythera; no page explains the drop, reviewer eu-01-a) plus six cells, two of them on the Halicarnassus peninsula in Turkey (lon 27.3-27.5, lat 37.1). No infobox area to compare. The page gives no settlement map for 1100-1000 BC ('The population of Greece declined'; Nichoria 'abandoned in 1150 BC but then reemerged as a small village cluster by 1075 BC'); the Halicarnassus cells are unverified: page budget. Attica, Euboea and central Crete 'recovered economically from these events faster than others'.

correction.text: the Greek mainland and Aegean islands, Crete and Cyprus as Cliopatria draws them, plus the Anatolian coast settled by the 'early movement from mainland Greece to the Anatolian coast' c. 1000 BC

keyframe_review.note: 60,722 km2: adds Cyprus (31 cells) and drops the Halicarnassus cells. The page dates the 'early movement from mainland Greece to the Anatolian coast' to c. 1000 BC, so the Anatolian coast (Ionia) should be added at this keyframe, not removed. Cyprus is kept at low confidence: 'Greek-speaking people arrived in Cyprus in the late 13th to 11th centuries BC, but did not colonize the island'; 'sub-Mycenaean Cyprus (c. 1100-1050 BC)'.

correction.text: the Greek mainland and Aegean islands, Crete and Cyprus as Cliopatria draws them, plus the Anatolian coast settled by the 'early movement from mainland Greece to the Anatolian coast' c. 1000 BC

keyframe_review.note: Unchanged from -1000 (60,722 km2); the same Ionia correction. The four Early Iron Age centres are Lefkandi, Athens, Argos and Knossos; Protogeometric 1050-900 BC, Early and Middle Geometric 900-800 BC; recovery 'was well underway by the beginning of the 8th century BC'.

region.text: 'Greek mainland and Aegean Sea' (infobox range): the mainland, Crete and the islands after the fall of the palaces

ledger.note: c. 1100 BCE: the Greek world enters the Dark Age. Infobox 'c. 1180-800 BC'; 'Mycenaean palaces began to come to an end around 1200 BC', with revolts 'c. 1200-1150 BC' and the fall 'attributed to a Dorian or Sea Peoples invasion'. Cliopatria's -1100 start is kept as the handover from Mycenaean Greece, whose page ends c. 1050.

c. 1000 BCE: Greeks from the mainland settle the Anatolian coast. The page's 'early movement from mainland Greece to the Anatolian coast' is dated 'perhaps as early as 1000 BC'; it names no cities, so the gazetteer's Ionia stands for the coast. Cliopatria's shape drops Anatolia at this date instead; the keyframe is corrected.

region.text: Cyprus, where 'Greek-speaking people arrived in Cyprus in the late 13th to 11th centuries BC'

ledger.note: c. 1000 BCE: Greek-speaking Cyprus is drawn with the Greek world on Cliopatria's date. The page: Greek speakers arrived 'in the late 13th to 11th centuries BC, but did not colonize the island'; 'sub-Mycenaean Cyprus (c. 1100-1050 BC)'; the Dorian invasion page notes the Arcadocypriot features shared by 'Arcadia in the Peloponnese and the island of Cyprus'. The Cypriot kingdoms (Alashiya and the Iron Age city-kingdoms) have no Cliopatria row, hence 'nobody'.

region.text: the Greek mainland, the islands, Crete, Cyprus and the Anatolian coast at the end of the Middle Geometric period

ledger.note: c. 800 BCE: the Dark Age ends and the age of the poleis begins. The period ends 'in the beginning of the Protohistoric Iron Age, c. 800 BC'; the oikoi are 'the origins of the later poleis'; 'By the beginning of 8th century BC, a new Greek alphabet system was adopted from the Phoenician alphabet'; 'the first Olympics, in 776 BC'.

certainty.note: No borders at all: the row is an archaeological period, drawn as the area of Greek settlement; the Anatolian coast and Cyprus are the softest, the Aegean coastlines sharp by nature.

sources.title: Greek Dark Ages
sources.note: Identity, dates (c. 1180-800 BC; Early Iron Age 1050-800), sub-periods, the four centres, the Anatolian movement c. 1000 BC, Cyprus, the end c. 800 BC and the Olympics of 776.

sources.title: Dorian invasion
sources.note: The Dorian migration as tradition and as 'a myth by most scholars'; Doric, Arcadocypriot and Ionic dialect geography; Attica and Euboea unaffected.

sources.title: Late Bronze Age collapse
sources.note: The collapse 'from c. 1200 BC to c. 800 BC' as the start of 'the Greek Dark Ages, which lasted roughly 400 years'; Cyprus's continuity after 1200 BC.

sources.title: Mycenaean Greece
sources.note: The end of the Mycenaean period c. 1050 BC; Athens's acropolis avoided destruction; refugees to Cyprus.

notes:
Written by the eu-01-a research agent on 2026-10-18 from two pages opened for this state (Greek Dark Ages, Dorian invasion; budget 1-2) and two shared with the Mycenaean dossier.

This row is a period, not a polity: the page describes 'independent regions organized by kinship groups and the oikoi' ruled by aristocrats, with no capital, ruler list or border. It is kept as one dossier of type 'state' because Cliopatria draws it and the scope wants the Greek world on the map between the palaces and the poleis; the orchestrator may prefer to render it muted. Athens is a label anchor, not a capital.

Dates: the page gives c. 1180-800 BC, the Mycenaean page ends c. 1050; Cliopatria's -1100..-801 is kept so the two dossiers meet at -1100 without a gap or overlap; the end -800 matches the page and Cliopatria's Greek City-States row (-800).

Cliopatria corrections: the -1000 and -900 shapes drop Anatolia while the page dates the movement to the Anatolian coast c. 1000 BC, so Ionia is added to both (adjust). Cyprus (added by Cliopatria at -1000) is kept at confidence 1 against the page's 'did not colonize the island'; the reviewer may remove it. The two Halicarnassus cells of the -1100 shape are unverified.

Counterparts needing dossiers: the Cypriot city-kingdoms (Alashiya and its Iron Age successors Salamis, Paphos, Kition; no Cliopatria row), the Ionian, Aeolian and Dorian foundations in Anatolia (Miletus, Ephesus, Smyrna, Halicarnassus, Rhodes, Kos) as dated foundations, which the scope assigns to batch eu-01-x. Not opened for want of budget: Lefkandi, Ionians, Protogeometric art, Archaic Greece. Gazetteer names lacking: Lefkandi, Argos (the place), Aeolis (region), Halicarnassus exists.
